data.exact_reserve_text: The underwriting result in 2019 was affected by catastrophe events mainly Hurricane Dorian, Typhoon Faxai and Typhoon Hagibis, as well as deterioration on prior year catastrophe events mainly Hurricane Irma. Collectively, these represented net losses of GBP 16,700k. There has also been significant prior year deterioration on Woodstock and Personal Accident that were discontinued in 2018 and Financial Lines, General Casualty and Hull.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's gross claims reserves opened at GBP 337.016m. Analysis of the gross claims development table shows an overall adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 45.8m (around 13.6% of opening reserves), driven by adverse development on older underwriting years (notably 2017 and 2016). Management attributes the deterioration primarily to prior-year catastrophe development (principally Hurricane Irma) and significant adverse movements on discontinued portfolios and lines including Woodstock, Personal Accident, Financial Lines, General Casualty and Hull. Additionally, 2019 catastrophe activity (Hurricane Dorian, Typhoon Faxai and Typhoon Hagibis) impacted the current year underwriting result and contributed to overall loss experience.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was not provided as a single explicit gross movement figure in the notes; the reported gross PYD has been calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative estimates) found in the Technical Provisions note. There is an RITC line present in the 2018 movements which can distort development patterns; care taken to exclude aggregated 'and prior' columns. Some narrative figures quoted in the report are net of reinsurance; where no gross quantification was given for specific events, amounts are left null. Confidence for the PYD is 0.8 because it is a calculated gross total from the triangle.
